x: Belgrave's second placed team in the Crawley Road Relay. Left to Right: John Stowe, Richard Langley, Pat Breslin and Bill Curtin.
John Stowe produced a really good run on the firsr leg to finish 5th and Peter Carton stepped up the rhythm even faster to hand over in 3rd place.
A below par Bill Curtin was drawn in the same heat of the 1500 metres as John Stowe but neither made the final---Bill being 4th (4:09.4) and John 5th (4:11.2).

Gerry North gave his injury a good try-out, although he still surprised some of the middle of the field by finishing faster than he started. Note should also be made of youths, Peter Carton and John Stowe who both finished in very good times and look to have bright futures.
The shape of things to come was shown by Bill Curtin and John Stowe (both Youths) placing 11th and 12th---John scooping the handicap to boot!.
Richard Langley, still a boy, showed his paces by beating that useful trio Binda, Butcher and Harris and getting within 17 seconds of John Stowe.

John Stowe was only 120 yards further back with Tony Binda a similar distance behind John, but closing fast. Our Press Honorary Secretary, Don Maclean, was an interested spectator as he was a winner of this race in the early 1950's.

Full of congratulations for Peter we just caught the back of John Stowe going away for the second leg. We thought that we had had our moment of glory and that John, although he would always try his best, must lose several places during his stint.

With Carton and Curtin grimly hanging on to their places around the twenty mark, John Stowe going well in the early sixties and Tony Binda only another twenty places back, a count at two miles placed us second, yes second.
We also Have John Boardman, Mel Ford and another junior, John Stowe, under the 2 minute barrier and Colin Pearson and John Kelly should also be shortly.
It's 14th February 1970 and Tony Binda takes over from John Stowe at the start of stage three of the Mitcham Young Athletes Relay in Morden Park.
